comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was substantially heavier and incurred collision cleanup, but both completed and failed equally, so the budget difference is not an outcome-differential explanation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations make this a both_fail pair: parallel and serial each passed 3 of 70 official cases and solution_passed is false. Both attempts recognized the same task and built similar ESM Bech32/CLI translations with representative local parity checks. The concrete task-solving difference is that parallel delegated probes and implementation into live children that also wrote the shared /output tree, forcing interruption and cleanup of overlapping entrypoint/module work; serial kept all work in one actor and avoided that coordination cost. Because the official scores are identical and hidden evaluator failures are not exposed in the pair, the retained parallel coordination defect is an adverse process consequence, not a proven cause of an outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Parallel produced overlapping /output implementations from root and child agents and had to reconcile duplicate modules before finalizing.
Parallel still completed selected verification and final delivery, but official evaluation failed 3/70.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided delegation and wrote one coherent output tree after local probing.
Serial also failed official evaluation 3/70, so its linear workflow did not solve the hidden task coverage gap.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions likely shared an implementation-coverage limitation not exposed by the selected local probes; the pair data gives only aggregate official failure, not hidden testcase diffs.
The visible program-name difference in CLI text was treated as expected by both agents and does not explain the official 3/70 score.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an evidenced parallel adverse process effect, not an exclusive root cause
